key_insight: 3D opto-electro-thermal simulations show that lead-free MgXS3 (X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites can deliver high-efficiency solar cells when absorber thickness, doping, defects, and an Sb2S3 BSF are jointly optimized.
engineering_relevance: The study provides device-design guidance for replacing toxic Pb-based absorbers with thermally robust, high-performance chalcogenide perovskites in realistic solar-cell architectures.
method: Built a ZnSe/MgXS3/Sb2S3 solar-cell model in COMSOL Multiphysics.
Coupled optical generation, drift-diffusion transport, and heat transfer under AM 1.5G illumination.
Swept absorber thickness, doping, defect density, and BSF effects for Ti, Zr, and Hf variants.
evidence_signal: Optimized simulations reported PCEs of 28.18% (MgZrS3), 26.72% (MgTiS3), and 28.16% (MgHfS3), with corresponding VOC, JSC, and FF values showing strong device performance.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based, so experimental validation and sensitivity to fabrication defects, interfaces, and material parameter uncertainty remain necessary.
paper_title: Numerical exploration on unveiling the photovoltaic potential of MgXS3(X = Ti, Zr, Hf) chalcogenide perovskites
